This paper introduces a circular enumeration method for labeled binary trees with $n$ leaves, ensuring that consecutive encoded trees differ only in the direction (left/right orientation) of a single edge. This approach extends existing circular methods applicable to complete $k$-ary trees to accommodate general structures, utilizing a specific labeling called a "structured labeling." Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that this code supports efficient computation and retrieval of successor states, with operations requiring $O(n)$ time and $O(n)$ storage.

The upcoming sPHENIX upgrade aims to enhance the detector's capabilities for heavy-ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). A key component of this upgrade involves integrating a novel silicon inner tracker (ACTs), designed to improve tracking precision and vertexing efficiency. This silicon device will supplement the existing central drift chambers and inner calorimeters. This paper outlines the software framework developed to incorporate ACTs data into the existing sPHENIX track reconstruction process. We detail the performance of this framework using high-purity proton-lead and gold-gold collision datasets recorded during 2014, specifically focusing on the reconstruction of muon decay electrons. The results indicate that adding ACTs data substantially enhances track-fitting accuracy and improves vertexing capabilities.

This work introduces a novel approach to computing the temporal jump term within space-time finite element methods for parabolic problems, utilizing a technique that projects the jump term across degrees of freedom along temporal directions. By employing a temporal interpolation strategy that requires no specific constraints, the proposed method achieves superior efficiency compared to conventional approaches that depend on nodal solution data. Theoretical analysis confirms that this method maintains the optimal order accuracy inherent to the space-time formulation. Furthermore, numerical experiments are provided to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the algorithm's efficiency.

This paper investigates circular flows and their relationship to T-joins in unidirected signed graphs. We present and analyze two distinct circulation flow models for these graphs, tailored to the constraints of positive and negative edges. We derive specific criteria for when circular flows exist in these signed graphs and demonstrate that these conditions are equivalent to the existence of T-joins within them. Furthermore, we establish that the minimum magnitude of a circular flow in any graph is 1, and that the minimum circular flow for signed graphs is always an even number.

The subset sum problem involves determining whether a specific target can be formed by summing a subset of integers from a given collection. This paper addresses the deterministic case where an input array consists of $n$ integers from $\{1, \dots, n^2\}$ and the target equals $n^2$. We present an algorithm with a running time of $O(n^{1.15})$, achieving a significant speedup over the previously best-known deterministic approach of $O(n^{2/3})$. Our method relies on a new technique for solving modular subset problems, which may benefit other areas of research.

The study of hemocyte migration in Drosophila melanogaster embryos offers a model for understanding how cells navigate in three-dimensional environments. By tracking hemocytes in real-time, researchers can analyze their movement patterns, specifically the "tango" phenomenon where cells reverse direction. The authors introduce a novel method to quantify the characteristics of these turns and demonstrate that the frequency of direction changes is not random; instead, it is modulated by the cell's speed. This finding suggests that hemocyte navigation is not merely a random walk but a structured process. The paper concludes by discussing the biological implications of these observations.

This paper introduces an innovative semi-supervised speech recognition framework utilizing a contrastive twin network. The approach leverages extensive data from a pretrained automatic speech recognition model to enhance performance with limited labeled audio. The framework employs a twin encoder to generate audio embeddings, which are then subjected to contrastive learning to ensure that the resulting embeddings align closely with those derived from the audio segments in the corresponding labeled sentences. The final decoder utilizes a combination of these twin encoder embeddings and the text from the labeled sentences to produce word sequences. Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 20.5% relative improvements in Word Error Rate (WER) compared to fully supervised training, reducing the relative error from 29.4% to 23.5% when using only 10% of the training data.

This paper details the 2021 revisions to the framework functions for inelastic lepton-nucleon scattering, incorporating recent advancements in nucleon structure knowledge. We introduce a new axial framework function, $F_A$, and update the vector ones, $F_1$ and $F_2$, to reflect the latest insights into nucleon spin and momentum distributions. These improvements integrate recent global analyses for nucleon structure, including the JAM, RHIC, and NNPDF datasets. We also provide the framework function for the $Z^0$ boson, $F_Z$, and update the associated numerical tables and plots to ensure consistency with our recent research.

The brain's ability to process information is characterized by its multi-factor and multi-modal nature. While the human brain is adept at integrating various factors and sensory modalities, it also excels in handling diverging time scales, such as the shift from immediate to long-term goals. However, existing computational frameworks often fail to account for these combined complexities. To address this, we introduce a new theoretical model termed Multi-Modal and Multi-Factor Diverging Time Active Inference (MMMF-TII). This model integrates diverging time scales, multiple factors, and multiple modalities to explain how the brain processes complex, multi-faceted information. We demonstrate that the model can effectively simulate key human behaviors, including the interplay between short-term and long-term planning, as well as the relationship between perception and action. Furthermore, we show that the model can be trained using only unsupervised data, making it a versatile and robust framework for understanding human information processing.

This study examines the formation of Korteweg-de Vries solitons within a cold quark-gluon plasma, specifically within a regime where the system is treated as a relativistic, ideal fluid. The analysis reveals that the Korteweg-de Vries approximation remains valid only when the soliton's velocity is sufficiently low. Under these conditions, an analytical formula is derived for the amplitude of the Korteweg-de Vries solitons.

While such families are well-documented in physics, particularly concerning harmonic oscillators, this paper investigates the conditions under which a vector field exhibits isochronic behavior. We demonstrate that a vector field with isochronous properties must be derived from a harmonic oscillator. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between the vector field and the potential of the corresponding harmonic oscillator.

This paper examines the properties of L\'{a}bels as a linearized approximation (LAN) across various families of distributions derived from solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by Levy processes. Specifically, we investigate how the local behavior of this families changes under specific asymptotic conditions.

We demonstrate that the spectrum of the Laplace operator on a flat surface is uniquely determined by its Teichmüller class, provided the surface is either g-generic or has genus one. This result extends a previous demonstration by the first author, which established such spectral determination solely for almost every surface in the Teichmüller modular group. Furthermore, we prove that for surfaces of genus greater than one, the length spectrum of geodesics on those surfaces is a spectral invariant. This finding broadens a discovery by Kolpakov, which previously showed this invariance holds for a full measure subset within the respective Teichmüller modular group.

We introduce FNetAR, a streamlined autoregressive architecture that merges Fourier transform principles with tokenization to establish a superior, efficient, and effective alternative to autoregressive Transformers. By utilizing tokens to represent frequency domain data, FNetAR enables the use of autoregression for prediction, allowing it to match the performance of Transformers across various sequence lengths. Furthermore, FNetAR offers a superior theoretical foundation for modeling time series, as it can be interpreted as a linear autoregressive process within the Fourier domain. This model is further enhanced by its ability to support exact Bayesian inference, a capability that facilitates precise uncertainty quantification.

This study examines a cosmological framework where the dark energy component is modeled as a generalized ghost traveler scalar field, adhering to the Saez-Ballester metric for scalar-tensor gravity. We derive the governing equations for the scale factor, the scalar field, and the equation of state, subsequently analyzing their asymptotic behaviors at both late and early times. Furthermore, we determine the stability of the model's solutions and discuss their physical implications.

This study examines a scenario where multiple users compete to order virtual network functions (VNFs) from a multi-access edge computing (MEC) platform. The VNFs are hosted on multiple MEC servers, each constrained by limited resources. The VNFs are categorized into three types: caching, computation, and backhaul. The caching and computation functions are user-specific, while the backhaul function is common across all users. The primary goal of the users is to minimize their end-to-end latency, which depends on the selected VNFs, the specific server chosen, and the number of concurrent users on that server. The number of users directly impacts the completion time of the VNFs. This paper introduces a mean-field game (MFG) model to represent user behavior and employs a reinforcement learning approach to train agents for identifying optimal user strategies. The findings indicate that the proposed reinforcement learning method effectively trains agents to converge toward the MFG equilibrium.

We investigate a renormalization group analysis of a two-dimensional Dirac fermion system incorporating random random mass terms. Our findings indicate that the system exhibits a non-Gaussian fixed point characterized by a relevant random field direction. Through one-loop corrections, we determine the critical exponent for the random mass correlation and establish a condition for the stability of this fixed point. Furthermore, we demonstrate that, within the limit of a small fermion bandwidth, the system's critical behavior is defined by a fixed point with random fluctuations in the mass distribution.

Depression is a prevalent mental health condition that significantly impacts individuals' daily functioning and quality of life. Although the majority of research has concentrated on the negative aspects of this disorder, there is a growing interest in understanding the positive events experienced by those living with depression. This study examines the self-reported happy moments of individuals with depression, utilizing text data from an online support group for the condition. We employ a novel approach to identify these moments by analyzing the interplay between sentiment and topic, and we explore the types of positive experiences reported by these individuals. Our findings reveal that while events classified as happy are often personal and subjective, they can also be categorized as happy based on negative occurrences due to contextual factors.

This work examines the breaking of isospin symmetry in Sp(4) gauge theory featuring a single Dirac fermion in the fundamental representation, utilizing lattice simulations. We introduce a new lattice action that ensures exact preservation of isospin symmetry alongside nearly perfect near-continuum behavior. By analyzing the spectrum of two-point correlation functions for vector and axial-vector currents, we establish that this action effectively mitigates isospin breaking effects. Furthermore, we compute the decay constants for $F$ and $D$ mesons, observing that the ratio $R = f_F/f_D$ exceeds the value of 2. These results indicate that the $1/R$ scaling predicted by the $1/N$ expansion is incorrect, suggesting instead that isospin breaking in this model is robust.

We report on the crystal structure, magnetic behavior, and electronic properties of Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$, a new nickel tellurate featuring $\mathit{S}$ = 1 chains. This material exhibits a composition of $\delta$ = 0.25, containing 93.75% Ni$^{2+}$ ions. The Ni$^{2+}$ ions form zigzag chains with a chain-to-chain distance of 4.101(1) \AA\ and a chain-to-chain angle of 109.3(1)$^\circ$. The Ni$^{2+}$ moments are antiferromagnetically coupled within these zigzag chains, a phenomenon driven by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. The observed magnetic susceptibility follows a two-sublattice model, displaying a broad maximum at 10 K. Furthermore, the specific heat data reveals a broad peak at 10 K, attributed to the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

Smart vehicular networks (SVNs) are poised to transform the global transportation sector by leveraging advanced technologies to enhance safety, efficiency, and sustainability. However, the integration of these technologies introduces significant challenges, primarily regarding the secure and reliable interconnection of vehicles with cloud computing, communication systems, and other smart devices. Consequently, ensuring trust in SVN operations is paramount for their successful deployment. This paper introduces a conceptual framework designed to govern trust within uncertain SVN environments. By synthesizing existing research on SVN trust and governance, the study outlines the core elements of an SVN, categorizes its constituent technologies, and examines the trust implications associated with each. Furthermore, the paper analyzes existing trust models and governance strategies, identifying their limitations when applied to uncertain SVN contexts. Finally, the work proposes a conceptual governance framework for managing trust in such networks and outlines the necessary research directions to advance the field.

We introduce a method for the consistent and monotone estimation of functions $f$ that possess a strong, monotone derivative, a property known as a Lipschitz-continuous derivative. This methodology leverages a new class of functions defined by a cubic polynomial on each interval of a specific partition, with monotonicity determined by the derivative's behavior at the partition points. We establish a convergence rate of $O(n^{-2/3})$ for these functions, which is optimal given the availability of only $n$ data points. This approach is particularly valuable in scenarios where monotonicity is crucial, such as in the analysis of gene expression data.

We introduce a novel class of static, axisymmetric Taub-NUT black hole solutions within a theory featuring a non-minimally coupled scalar field. These solutions are derived from a regular Taub-NUT spacetime filled with regular matter, utilizing a specific ansatz for the scalar field that generates a smooth, periodic axis. While the original axis remains regular, the process involves "pinching off" segments of alternating length, $\pi l$, to form a chain of topological $Z_2$-symmetric black loops. We demonstrate that this transformation yields a discontinuous spectrum of Taub-NUT parameter values, resulting in a Taub-NUT black hole configuration that is not in one-to-one correspondence with the loops. Furthermore, we establish that the scalar field does not alter the horizon's topological structure, which remains $S^2\times S^1$, and we confirm that the scalar field is essential for the existence of these loop solutions.

Facilitating the manual annotation of audio with extensive taxonomies is essential for creating sound-based knowledge bases, yet it remains a challenging task. This difficulty arises because annotators must constantly toggle between extensive lists of sound categories and the audio itself, a process that is prone to errors and inefficient. To address this, we introduce a new framework that streamlines the tagging workflow. This system allows the user to select a category and extract all its instances from the audio, enabling the user to verify and modify results before applying the label. We evaluated this approach through a study involving the tagging of 100 hours of environmental audio using a six-class taxonomy. The results demonstrated that our method significantly enhances both annotation efficiency and accuracy.

This study introduces a novel approach to model the dynamics of complex adaptive systems by integrating the principles of dynamical mean-field theory (Dynamical Cavity Theory) with the framework of dynamical systems. The method is applied to a representative system: a population of organisms colonizing a patchy environment. In this scenario, each organism can either remain in its current patch or migrate to a neighboring one, with the latter option being restricted to a specific set of patches. The system is defined by the probability that any given patch is inhabited. The central challenge is to determine the time evolution of these probabilities, which depends on the collective behavior of the entire population.

By applying a mean-field approximation, the problem is reduced to a set of coupled ordinary differential equations. The solution reveals that the system's behavior is governed by a single parameter, $\alpha$, which represents the ratio of the migration rate to the local growth rate. The dynamics are characterized by a phase transition occurring at a critical value of $\alpha = 1$. When $\alpha < 1$, the system exhibits a stable, homogeneous state where all patches are equally populated. Conversely, when $\alpha > 1$, the system undergoes a phase transition to a stable, heterogeneous state where some patches remain empty while others become densely populated.

We investigate the statistical characteristics of avalanche magnitudes within a branching process defined by a constant number of offspring per site. The analysis employs a straightforward argument to derive the avalanche probability distribution, demonstrating that it follows a power law with an exponent determined by the branching ratio. This result aligns with findings from previous studies that utilized both the critical probability distribution and the avalanche size distribution.

Although current discourse parsing systems excel at identifying sentence boundaries and connecting them through specific relations, they often fail to ensure these outputs align with human understanding of context. This study introduces a unified framework that integrates discourse parsing with question-answering to test whether a system genuinely grasps the nuances of its representations. By using natural queries to evaluate parsed sentences, this approach assesses whether the connections identified reflect actual contextual meaning. We demonstrate that when a system can answer queries based on discourse representations, it necessitates a rigorous and meaningful understanding of the relationships between those sentences.

This review examines the application of Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs) to hyperbolic wave transmission problems. It begins by outlining the PML methodology for both damped and perfect hyperbolic equations, highlighting the specific challenges posed by hyperbolicity. The discussion then addresses the numerical discretization of these PML-integrated equations, covering finite difference, finite element, and spectral methods. Furthermore, the text explores the implementation of PMLs within finite difference time domain (FDTD) schemes and their role in stabilizing explicit time-stepping. Finally, the review covers PML applications in acoustic and elastodynamic simulations, concluding with an analysis of key theoretical and numerical results derived from existing literature.

This study examines the interaction between laser pulses and droplets to achieve controlled modification and fragmentation of droplet clusters. The laser's characteristics, specifically pulse duration and energy, are pivotal in determining the droplet array's final state. We introduce a novel method to alter droplet configurations by employing a laser pulse to melt the junctions between adjacent droplets, thereby enabling their subsequent movement.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a ubiquitous paradigm that connects physical objects to the Internet, enabling them to communicate and share data. However, the massive influx of IoT traffic introduces significant challenges for network operators, who must ensure that data is delivered efficiently and with minimal latency. To address these issues, we introduce a novel orchestration structure that integrates Software-Defined Networking (SDN) within a Publish/Subscribe architecture. This approach leverages the dynamic capabilities of both SDN and the flexibility of the messaging model to optimize traffic flow. We developed this orchestration tool to manage the specific needs of an IoT-based smart agriculture system, where data from various sensors is aggregated and distributed to relevant stakeholders. Simulation results indicate that our orchestration structure effectively manages the network, delivering superior performance in terms of throughput and latency.

The LkH$\alpha\,330$ system, a young T Tauri star exhibiting strong H$\alpha$ emission, is a prime candidate for hosting a planetary system. We present new observations of the disk's structure and composition, utilizing high-resolution spectroscopy and polarimetry of scattered light alongside millimeter-wave continuum data. These observations reveal a complex architecture featuring a prominent inner cavity, a secondary gap, and a substantial outer disk. Furthermore, the disk contains a high density of small dust grains, a phenomenon linked to the intense stellar activity. We propose that the inner cavity is carved by a protoplanet with a mass of approximately 10 Earth masses ($10\,M_{\rm Jup}$), while the secondary gap is attributed to a second planet with a mass of roughly 1 Earth mass ($1\,M_{\rm Jup}$). The presence of a large reservoir of small grains suggests that this second body is currently undergoing active accretion. Finally, the disk's complex morphology and the system's overall characteristics indicate that LkH$\alpha\,330$ represents a young planetary system in a formative stage.

We establish novel concepts for distance metrics and gyrocalculus within the domain of symmetric positive definite matrices, leveraging existing normed vector space definitions. These concepts generalize current conceptions of normed distances and the gyrocalculus framework. Our work derives key properties for these new metrics and presents the corresponding metric epilogue. Additionally, we examine how these distances relate to the standard-induced norm distance and analyze whether norm-induced norm epilogue holds in this context. Finally, we explore these new metrics' ability to define a gradient on the domain of symmetric positive definite matrices, contrasting this with the traditional gradient framework.

The European Union has established ambitious goals for decarbonization, necessitating a shift from fossil fuels to hydrogen in sectors like transportation, industry, and power generation. This study examines the economic and environmental benefits of a European hydrogen network, modeled as a network of interconnected pipelines. We utilize a mixed-integer linear programming approach to determine the optimal network design, accounting for the system's operational costs, infrastructure investment, and existing natural gas pipelines. Our results indicate that the proposed hydrogen network can lower the total cost of hydrogen production by 10% and reduce carbon emissions by 20%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the network's efficiency is highly sensitive to the location of hydrogen sources and the demand for it at specific points.

This study examines the impact of a horizontal magnetic field on the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves traveling vertically through a conductive medium. We establish that a horizontal magnetic field induces anisotropy in wave propagation, resulting in different transit times for waves polarized parallel versus perpendicular to the field. We further demonstrate that this differential transit time can be utilized to identify the presence and strength of the field within such conductors. Additionally, we show that the magnitude of this anisotropic time difference increases with the depth of the magnetic field relative to the surface. These findings suggest a novel approach for detecting and quantifying horizontal magnetic fields using EM induction techniques.

Photonic chips are increasingly utilized to generate squeezed light, which is a quantum state of the vacuum that exhibits reduced noise in a specific quadrature. However, the stability of squeezing in these systems is compromised by photon loss, which degrades the output. This study demonstrates that squeezing can be protected against loss through the application of topological principles. We introduce a topological lattice designed to produce squeezed light while inherently resisting losses. Our findings reveal that the squeezing performance in this topological regime remains robust even when faced with loss rates as high as 10%. Furthermore, the topological lattice is simple to implement on integrated silicon nitride chips. This approach offers a promising pathway for developing practical, integrated quantum photonic devices.

This study addresses the fluid time optimal trajectory problem for a constant-thrust drone operating under uniform gravity, with a primary focus on minimizing maneuver duration. We introduce a novel geometric framework for trajectory planning that leverages the interplay between the system's natural dynamics and the optimal control Hamiltonian. By utilizing this perspective, we derive necessary conditions for optimality and construct trajectories that are provably optimal for specific scenarios. Furthermore, we develop a new method for calculating the complete set of solutions to a system of nonlinear equations, which are required to determine optimal trajectories. This approach is validated through a case study of a quadrotor executing a transition from hovering to forward flight.

This paper examines the algebraic structure of $q$-ary conjugate cyclic codes within a finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ along with their generator polynomials. It further investigates their algebraic composition, defines a specific class of these $q$-ary conjugate cyclic codes over the subfield $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, and establishes the weight enumerators for the resulting codes.

This thematic group report, compiled by experts from diverse backgrounds including experimentalists, theorists, and computational specialists, outlines the current state and future trajectory of careers within Community Engagement Frontier (CEF) sectors. It addresses the challenges faced by these communities, emphasizing the need for specific attention to underrepresented groups, particularly women and gender minorities. The document details the CEG's evolving career landscape, covering the roles of experimentalists, theorists, and computational specialists. Furthermore, it examines the impact of community engagement on high-energy physics and the associated challenges. Finally, the report presents strategic recommendations aimed at fostering a more inclusive and robust community engagement frontier.

This study presents an analysis of $W$ boson polarization within $t\bar{t}$ events using proton-proton collision data from the LHC at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ TeV, collected by the ATLAS detector with an integrated luminosity of 20.2 fb$^{-1}$. The investigation focuses on the dilepton decay channel of $t\bar{t}$ events, specifically the $W$-$W$ channel where the decay products of one $W$ boson form a jet. A maximum likelihood fit is applied to the angular distribution of the $W$ boson polarization, yielding a measured parameter $\alpha = 0.99 \pm 0.10$ (statistical) $\pm$ 0.04 (systematic). This result aligns with the Standard Model prediction of $\alpha = 1.0$.

This study reexamines the light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) for $D$ mesons, specifically focusing on the $D$-meson distribution amplitude (DA) defined on the heavy quark line. We investigate the DA's chiral structure, which is parameterized by three distinct components: the scalar chiral form $f_0$, the pseudoscalar chiral form $f_1$, and the chiral anomaly form $f_2$. Utilizing QCD sum rules, we determine the DA's normalization and its evolution with the renormalization scale. Our findings indicate that the scalar component $f_0$ dominates the DA, while the contributions from $f_1$ and $f_2$ are negligible.

Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The power hypergraph of $G$, denoted $P(G)$, is defined as a structure comprising $n$ vertices representing the original vertices of $G$ and $m$ hyperedges that correspond to $G$'s edges. The power hypernetwork, $P$, associated with $G$, is a diagonal matrix containing the degrees of the vertices of $G$ on its main diagonal, multiplied by an adjacency matrix representing $P(G)$. This work investigates the spectrum of the power hypernetwork, introducing a bound on its spectral radius dependent on the maximum degree of $G$ and the cardinality of its edges, while also deriving a lower bound for the minimum eigenvalue. Additionally, we examine the signed subgraph, a concept where a graph $G$ is assigned a binary weight to each edge, and we determine the conditions under which the smallest eigenvalue of this signed configuration is negative.

The Starlink network, operated by SpaceX, is a satellite constellation designed to deliver broadband internet access globally. While its primary function is communication, the system's growing popularity suggests it could also serve as an alternative to GPS for positioning. This paper examines the Starlink network's potential for localisation by analyzing its satellite geometry and signal transmission properties. It establishes theoretical performance boundaries for the system, specifically focusing on the relationship between satellite visibility and the achievable localisation accuracy. The study also investigates how these boundaries shift under different operational scenarios, including the presence of signal blockages and jamming. The results indicate that, despite these constraints, the system can support localisation with a mean relative error of 10⁻⁴, a level of precision that is sufficient for numerous practical applications.

We report the discovery of Transit Timing Variations (TTVs) in the Hot Jupiter XO-3b, which exhibit an amplitude of 10.5 ± 0.4 minutes. This variation is consistent with a third-body perturber, likely a massive companion planet, located at a semi-major axis of 0.21 ± 0.01 AU. The system's architecture is characterized by a high orbital eccentricity of 0.51 ± 0.05, a value that is inconsistent with standard Kozai-Lidov dynamics. Instead, the eccentricity likely stems from tidal interactions between the planet and its host star. We propose that the TTVs observed in XO-3b are a direct consequence of the planet's orbital evolution as it undergoes tidal circularization.

The 21-cm global signal offers a promising avenue for investigating the Universe's earliest epochs. However, extracting this signal from radio frequency interference (RFI) and foreground contamination remains a significant challenge. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian framework for signal wave calibration, which utilizes prior information to constrain the signal wave calibration matrix. We demonstrate that this method can effectively recover the signal from simulated data, even in scenarios with substantial foreground contamination. Furthermore, we show that it enables precise estimation of the signal wave calibration matrix, allowing for accurate recovery of the global signal's power spectrum.

We demonstrate that the Fock space comprising genus-zero, point-based Gromov–Witten invariants of $\mathbb{P}^N$ forms a coeval module over the ring of symmetric functions, with the covalent action governed by a generalized Giambelli formula. This result encompasses and extends the findings of Okounkov and Pandharipande regarding the coeval structure of genus-zero descendent Hodge integrals.

This study introduces a highly consistent (HCONS) framework for the number of primes within intervals $[1, x]$. By utilizing the HCONS property, we establish an enhanced approximation for Riemann's zero-counting function, $\Pi(T)$, achieving a precision level of $O(\log T)$. Furthermore, we derive the error term associated with the integral representation of $\Pi(T)$, demonstrating an accuracy of $O(\log t)$. These findings provide further support for the Riemann Hypothesis.

This paper introduces an approach utilizing natural cubic splines to analyze Alzheimer's disease clinical trials. The study addresses the specific challenge of handling a vast array of risk factors, where the primary goal is to identify which factors significantly influence the progression of the disease. Natural cubic splines are employed to model the non-linear relationship between a factor and the hazard rate, which is defined as the probability that a patient will develop the condition. The study evaluates the effectiveness of applying these splines in model selection and demonstrates their superiority over standard Cox regression models.

This paper introduces a novel method for constructing a parking map by utilizing data from tires in motion. We model the tire as a four-wheel omnidirectional robot and develop a system to estimate tire slip angles from wheel velocities. By combining these slip angles with a dead-reckoning approach, we calculate the vehicle's trajectory. Furthermore, we present a crawling algorithm that identifies unexplored regions and directs the car toward parking them. Experiments conducted in both simulated and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness of this proposed approach.

Adversarial attacks are typically optimized by minimizing loss, yet recent research indicates that minimizing the minimum feature level (level minima) can be a superior alternative. This study investigates the conditions under which level minimization approaches are effective. We introduce a new methodology for analyzing these attacks and demonstrate that a level minimization approach succeeds if the data distribution is not heavily skewed. Furthermore, we identify a critical failure scenario: when the loss function is non-differentiable, level minimization can be ineffective.

This paper introduces a reflective parametric frequency selective attenuator (RPFSA) that leverages the power modulation of a Josephson junction (JJ) to induce modulation in a transmission line's impedance. This approach enables the generation of highly tunable, narrowband attenuation across a frequency spectrum. The design achieves exceptionally low loss, utilizing a junction pair with minimal signal insertion loss of less than 0.01 dB, while maintaining a threshold power level below 1 microwatt. The device operates with a narrowband rejection greater than 20 dB and a passband loss under 1 dB, all while being fully tunable.

This study examines the SEIRS epidemic model under the extreme assumption of zero acquired immunity. In this framework, individuals transition from the Susceptible category to the Exposed category at a rate of $\mu$, representing the birth rate. After an incubation period lasting $\tau$ days, Exposed individuals move to the Infected category at a rate of $1/\tau$. The model further incorporates a time-dependent infection rate, $\beta(t)$, which is linked to the basic reproduction number $R_0(t)$. Once an individual is Infected, they are treated as Recovered after a duration of $\tau^*$ days, during which they remain isolated. The model accounts for the fact that Infected individuals may bypass quarantine and enter the population of Susceptibles at a rate of $\alpha(t)$. Additionally, Recovered individuals lose their immunity at a rate of $\mu_1$, returning to the Susceptible group. The dynamics of the system are governed by the following equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{S}(t) &= \mu - \mu S(t) + \alpha(t)I(t) - \mu_1SR(t) \\
E(t) &= \frac{1}{\tau}S(t) \\
I(t) &= \frac{1}{\tau}E(t) \\
R(t) &= \frac{1}{\tau^*}I(t) \\
I(t)

Word embeddings have become a cornerstone of natural language processing, with the quality of a word vector determined by its training context. While the optimal context varies by application, the most effective method for selecting a context remains unclear. This study evaluates context choices for three prominent models—GloVe, Word2Vec, and FastText—across three datasets (Twitter, Wikipedia, and Reddit) using four distinct methods: the original methods of GloVe, Word2Vec, and FastText, along with two newly proposed techniques. We assess these approaches using both intrinsic metrics, such as cosine similarity for word analogies, and extrinsic metrics, including word similarity and machine translation accuracy. Our findings indicate that context selection strategies significantly impact model performance and that, in most cases, a custom context yields superior results compared to the default settings provided by standard tools.

This paper investigates the maximum clique number $\omega(G)$ and $k$-clique number $r_k(G)$ within high-intensity random geometric graphs $G \sim {\rm RGG}(n, r_n)$, where $n$ denotes the vertex count and $r_n$ scales with $n$. We establish that for any fixed $k \geq 3$, the probability of $G$ containing a $k$-clique vanishes as $n \to \infty$, provided $r_n$ satisfies specific growth conditions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the ratio $\omega(G)/r_k(G)$ is bounded above by a constant that depends solely on $k$. These findings extend and refine prior work by Angel et al. (2019) and Angel and Peres (2020).

We introduce a Lagrangian framework for rotating stars, derived from a variational principle applied to the action integral. This approach yields the complete set of hydrodynamic and mass conservation equations, alongside the angular momentum transport equation, all of which are consistent with established literature. By solving the resulting Euler equations, we can determine the angular velocity profile within the star. Furthermore, we demonstrate that angular momentum transport can be modeled via an effective viscosity, which is defined by a specific constitutive law.

This study investigates the Palatini $f(R)$ gravity framework, specifically focusing on a spherically symmetric, pressureless dust model defined by $f(R) = R + \alpha R^n$. We derive the modified field equations and establish the corresponding constraints for this scenario. By applying a perturbative approach, we determine the metric function $A(r,t)$ and the areal radius $R(t,r)$, expressing them in terms of the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) solutions. Our analysis reveals that the perturbations of $A$ and $R$ depend on the parameter $\alpha$ and its derivatives, with the first-order terms in $\alpha$ vanishing. Consequently, the perturbations are of the order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi solution remains a valid solution to the field equations when $\alpha$ is sufficiently small.

Quantum nonlocality, a cornerstone of quantum information theory, is typically investigated using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states and their variants. However, these states are fragile against noise, which hinders their utility in practical applications. This work introduces a new class of $N$-partite quantum states that exhibit nonlocality under GHZ measurements while demonstrating resilience against noise. We present a robust quantum advantage in local discrimination among local unitary operations for these states, an advantage that persists even in noisy environments. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these local distinguishable states possess a local indistinguishable property. Our findings offer novel perspectives on the application of quantum nonlocality and suggest that the proposed states hold significant promise for future quantum communication technologies.

Web user gaze data serves as a critical indicator of human behavior and attention within digital environments. However, analyzing such data is often hindered by its inherent complexity, high dimensionality, and significant noise levels. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel approach for forecasting web visual attention that operates on short-duration windows. This forecasting model utilizes a sliding window technique to continuously predict attention levels across all image regions. The window is partitioned into segments, with each segment assigned a specific feature vector. These vectors are then processed by a deep learning architecture to generate the final forecast. We validated this approach using a comprehensive dataset comprising 1,000 sessions from 100 participants interacting with 10 distinct websites. The findings demonstrate that our method achieves high accuracy in forecasting web visual attention over short temporal intervals.

This paper introduces the transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS), a novel device for enhancing wireless communications. Unlike conventional reflective surfaces, TRIS units pass signals through at specific frequencies while blocking others, offering significant advantages in coverage and capacity. The work begins by outlining the fundamental principles of TRIS technology and its potential applications in future 6G networks. Subsequently, we present a functional prototype and validate its efficacy through experimental tests, including scenarios with obstructed line-of-sight links and simultaneous transmission of multiple signals on different frequencies. The results confirm that the prototype can selectively transmit desired signals while blocking specific frequencies, thereby demonstrating the practical viability of TRIS for future wireless systems.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves learning a policy from a static dataset without further environment interaction. This work examines the linear optimization framework for offline RL, which is designed to handle a broad class of linear function approximators. We demonstrate that this approach is versatile, capable of supporting a wide range of value function estimators, including both value-based and policy-gradient methods. Our analysis establishes that the framework achieves the optimal minimax regret bound for these estimators, a result that is new for many cases. Furthermore, we introduce a new offline RL algorithm that attains the same optimal performance guarantees by utilizing a linear combination of the outputs generated by these estimators.

This article introduces an elementary demonstration that the category of topological spaces equipped with free homotopy between maps is homotopically equivalent. This work offers an intuitive model space for analyzing invariant properties under conjugation within the realm of homotopy theory.

We present the first detection of a turbulent supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the distant galaxy J0437+2456. This discovery stems from a novel method that utilizes the central broad emission line (BLR) of active galactic nuclei (AGN) as a probe for SMBH dynamics. By analyzing the central broad component of the broad H$\beta$ line, we identified a central velocity dispersion of 1,000 km/s, which is significantly higher than the typical dispersion of 300 km/s observed in the outer BLR. This velocity profile indicates a central region dominated by a turbulent SMBH accretion disk. Furthermore, the central broad H$\beta$ component exhibits a velocity gradient of 1,000 km/s per kiloparsec, a steepness that suggests a turbulent accretion disk with a radius of approximately 100 parsecs. This turbulent disk is likely driven by a jet, which is supported by the detection of a 1.4 GHz radio jet in the host galaxy. This finding represents the first direct evidence of a turbulent SMBH accretion disk in a distant galaxy.

This paper examines planar restricted three-body configurations where the three massive bodies form a straight line, focusing specifically on the absence of self-collisions. We demonstrate that within any such configuration, the total mass of the three masses is bounded from above by $100/39$. Furthermore, we prove that if two bodies possess equal mass, their combined total mass cannot exceed $5/3$. Finally, we establish a lower bound of $1/2$ for the smaller mass among all three bodies.

Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) serves as a robust, quantitative tool for characterizing the local microenvironment of fluorophores. However, the optical aberrations inherent in microscope lenses can distort the acquired images, thereby compromising the precision of quantitative analysis. This study introduces a deconvolution approach to mitigate these optical artifacts in FLIM data. By modeling the microscope's point spread function (PSF) and convoluting it with a theoretical distribution of lifetimes, we constructed a system matrix for iterative reconstruction using Tikhonov regularization. This method effectively restores high-frequency components of the lifetime data, thereby enhancing spatial resolution. The efficacy of this technique was validated through the analysis of both synthetic FLIM datasets and experimental data from a commercial FLIM system.

Product search is a fundamental component of e-commerce, and customizing this experience for individual users is vital for enhancing engagement and driving sales. While existing methods typically rely on user and product attributes to generate recommendations, they often overlook the dynamic nature of user interactions. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that leverages graph convolution to capture user behavioral patterns. This model integrates both static data (such as demographic and preference profiles) and dynamic data (such as browsing and search history) into a graph structure, where nodes represent users, items, and features, and edges represent relationships. By applying graph convolution, we learn a comprehensive embedding for each user that synthesizes these diverse information sources. We validate the effectiveness of this approach through a case study with a leading e-commerce platform, demonstrating that it outperforms traditional methods that depend solely on static attributes.

Graph embedding is a critical technique for graph data analysis, yet existing methods often struggle with the dual challenges of handling noisy edges and the absence of explicit graph labels. To address these issues, we introduce the Unsupervised Deep Manifold Labeled Graph Embedding (UdMLGe), a novel framework that simultaneously learns graph embeddings and node representations. This approach begins by utilizing a manifold labeled graph constructed from the input graph to define a manifold structure, which is then transformed into a labeled graph within the latent space. Subsequently, we employ an unsupervised deep learning architecture to derive node embeddings and refine the labeled graph, followed by an objective function designed to maximize the alignment between these graph embeddings and node embeddings. Experimental results across various datasets confirm that UdMLGe outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in both graph embedding and node embedding tasks.

Non-orthogonal sequences are essential for enabling grant-free massive connectivity in fifth-generation (5G) networks. This paper introduces a novel design method for these sequences, structured in two stages: the first stage employs a genetic algorithm to generate an initial population of non-orthogonal sequences, while the second stage utilizes a second evolutionary process to evolve this population into a population of non-orthogonal codewords. The primary advantage of this two-stage design is the elimination of the need for a large initial random seed set, which significantly reduces the computational cost of the algorithm. Furthermore, the resulting sequences exhibit strong autocorrelation and low cross-correlation properties. Numerical simulations confirm that the proposed design is both effective and efficient.

This study introduces a novel encoder-blind combinatorial coded sensing architecture designed for applications involving numerous small targets. The proposed system comprises a straightforward linear encoder responsible for generating the sensing matrix and an intelligent decoder optimized for accurate target recovery. Specifically, the encoder employs a linear structure with sparsity constraints to create a sensing matrix capable of supporting compressed sensing, while the decoder utilizes a non-iterative algorithm to recover target locations based on the sensing measurements. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach achieves high accuracy in estimating target positions, while also offering superior simplicity and lower computational complexity compared to existing methods.

Domain adaptation seeks to enhance the performance of a model trained on a source domain when applied to a distinct target domain. While various techniques exist to address this challenge, the specific characteristics of the source and target domains often dictate the most effective strategy. This paper introduces a unified framework that leverages random transformations to bridge the source-target domain gap. By employing adversarial training, the model learns a domain-invariant representation capable of handling both domain adaptation and generalization to out-of-distribution data. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art results in domain adaptation and yields competitive performance in generalization tasks.

This paper establishes that any 2-local inner derivation acting on a Jordan algebra of matrices defined over a commutative involutive ring results in an actual inner derivation. Furthermore, it investigates conditions under which such 2-local representations hold for derivations on Jordan algebra elements.

This study examines the gravitational lensing effects on a Dirac singularity within Berry's phase. We find that the lensing deflection angle exhibits a discontinuity, featuring a jump of $2\pi$ at the photon sphere.

This study investigates the spin-orbit density dependence within compact solitons of Bose-Einstein condensates. We examine how the soliton's size and energy vary with spin-orbit coupling density, revealing that while the soliton's energy increases with this coupling density, its width remains constant for densities below a specific critical threshold. Beyond this threshold, further increases in coupling density cause the soliton's width to shrink. These findings highlight the spin-dependent dynamics of compact solitons in BECs, offering insights for controlling soliton formation and manipulation in spin-dependent contexts.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, which decays into $\Sigma_c(2455)^+\pi$, is recognized as the ground-state $\Lambda_c$ doublet with $J^P=1/2^+$. In contrast, the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$, which decays into $\Sigma_c(2520)^+\pi$, is identified as the first excited state of the $\Lambda_c$ doublet, possessing $J^P=3/2^+$. This study examines the decay of the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ into $\Sigma_c(2455)^+\pi$ and $\Sigma_c(2520)^+\pi$ by applying the heavy quark effective theory (HQET) and the $SU(3)$ flavor symmetry. The analysis reveals that the $\Sigma_c(2455)^+\pi$ channel is suppressed relative to the $\Sigma_c(2520)^+\pi$ channel, with a predicted suppression factor of approximately 0.1. Additionally, the branching ratio for $\Lambda_c(2625)^+\to\Sigma_c(2520)^+\pi$ is estimated to be roughly 0.1 times that of $\Lambda_c(2625)^+\to\Sigma_c(2520)^+\pi$. These findings are consistent with recent experimental measurements.

This work examines the $G$-orbital smoothness of functions on orbit spaces for compact Lie groups. We demonstrate that continuous functions on orbit spaces admit approximations via $G$-smooth continuous $G$-invariant functions on smooth, $G$-invariant orbifold submanifolds within a $G$-smooth manifold that serves as a manifold replacement for the tangent bundle of an orbifold structure on the orbit space. We also provide a counterexample showing that continuous $G$-invariant functions on smooth manifolds do not necessarily admit approximations via $G$-$C^\infty$ functions.

This position paper outlines the potential of future high-energy muon colliders to detect and investigate axion-like particles (ALPs). ALPs are hypothesized constituents of the dark sector, serving as viable dark matter candidates and potential explanations for the enigma of the strong CP problem. Their presence is suggested by numerous extensions to the Standard Model, and they are theorized to interact with photons and gluons through loop-induced couplings to fermions. While low-energy experiments have already placed constraints on these interactions, upcoming high-energy facilities offer the prospect of probing new physics at scales far beyond current reach. Muon colliders, in particular, provide a distinctive advantage by enabling the direct production of ALPs through the decay of off-shell W bosons. This study examines the anticipated sensitivity of a future muon collider to these particles, focusing on scenarios involving ALPs that couple exclusively to gluons and those with electromagnetic couplings mediated by charged fermions.

Metadata plays a critical role in the performance of modern storage systems, yet its importance is frequently overlooked. This paper introduces MetaSys, an open-source, flexible, and practical system designed to implement and assess cross-layer storage optimizations centered on metadata management. By offering a modular architecture, MetaSys allows for the rapid implementation, evaluation, and comparison of various metadata strategies. We detail the system's design and implementation, demonstrating its versatility through three distinct use cases: (1) optimizing CPU and memory usage via efficient data structures, (2) reducing latency through hardware-assisted acceleration, and (3) enhancing throughput by optimizing the distribution of metadata across multiple drives.

This paper introduces a novel method for transferring knowledge from a source domain to a target domain, leveraging synthetic data and Siamese networks. The proposed approach is evaluated against existing transfer learning strategies using the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques, particularly when applied to domains with limited sample sizes.

Recurrent neural networks (RRCNs) are a class of neural networks designed to handle sequential data. While they excel at modeling such inputs, they often struggle with retaining information over long periods. To address this, we introduce the Fourier Recurrent Unit (FRU), a new RNN architecture that leverages Fourier series to model temporal dependencies. We demonstrate that FRUs can be integrated seamlessly into any RNN framework. Furthermore, we introduce a novel gating mechanism that enables FRUs to adaptively determine the optimal Fourier series parameters for any given task. We validate the FRU's effectiveness across various tasks, including those requiring long-term memory, and show through experiments that it outperforms other methods in both accuracy and training speed.

This paper introduces a new approach to the optimal control problem within Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). We present a novel algorithm that identifies the optimal policy by traversing the MDP's state space, relying on the transition probabilities and reward function. By utilizing a graph-theoretic framework, the method calculates a "navigation score" for every state, defined as the accumulated reward along the most rewarding path leading to the optimal state. We demonstrate that the set of states with a non-zero score precisely corresponds to the reachable states under the optimal policy. Leveraging this insight, the algorithm identifies the optimal policy by zeroing out all states with a score of zero. We establish that the computational complexity of this approach is $O(|S^2|\cdot |A|)$, where $S$ represents the set of states and $A$ represents the set of actions.

We introduce a novel method for generating attosecond electron bunches utilizing the dual-wake injection technique. This approach involves injecting a primary electron bunch into a vacuum chamber containing a wakefield generated by a secondary, ultraperipheral heavy ion bunch. The resulting electron beam exhibits a duration of approximately 100 attoseconds, maintains a charge of roughly 100 femtocoulombs, and demonstrates a polarization degree exceeding 99%. Notably, the beam's energy spectrum is highly tunable, ranging from 10 MeV to over 100 GeV, with the ability to achieve a relative energy spread as low as 1%. These characteristics make the proposed method a highly promising avenue for developing ultra-high brightness, polarized attosecond electron sources.

This study explores the emergence of complexity in astrophysical contexts, beginning with the fundamental complexity of the early universe and tracing its development through the first stars, the formation of galaxies, and the birth of planets. We examine the specific conditions necessary for life to arise, while also analyzing the evolution of complexity within living systems and the subsequent rise of intelligence. The discussion concludes by considering the presence of life within our galaxy and beyond, within our observable universe, and potentially across the cosmos as a whole.

The escalating global concern regarding climate change has driven a surge in research and development, particularly within the field of computational science. This study examines the evolution of publications and research trends in climate change investigation over the last two decades by analyzing data from GitHub and ORCID. Our analysis reveals a marked increase in research output, which has become increasingly interdisciplinary. Furthermore, we identify a growing emphasis on open science practices, including the adoption of open-source code, data, and publications. However, a significant gap remains between the accessibility of open research materials and the standards required for effective policy-making. To address this, we propose a framework for extracting evidence-based insights for policy development from open repositories. This approach leverages AI to map author networks and trace the evolution of research groups, thereby supporting a robust foundation for R&D policy-making.

Android's widespread adoption in mobile devices has heightened the necessity for rigorous security assessments. While Side-Channel Analysis (SCA) is a common method for evaluating security, its application to the Android platform remains largely unexplored. This paper introduces ASVAAN, a semi-automated framework designed to facilitate SCA on the Android Native Development Kit (NDK). ASVAAN facilitates the construction of test platforms capable of executing specific operations while simultaneously gathering side-channel data, such as power consumption traces. By utilizing the open-source Android framework, the framework allows researchers to easily design custom test cases and measure corresponding side-channel signatures.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction for facilitating secure, decentralized, and transparent digital transactions. As the second-largest cryptocurrency network by total value locked, Ethereum serves as a critical infrastructure for decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts, enabling a wide array of services. This study introduces a novel approach to analyzing the temporal dynamics of the transaction network within the Ethereum blockchain. We utilize ego-networks to examine the local structural properties of individual node interactions over time. By integrating node metadata—including labels derived from dApps, the Ethereum Foundation, and the Golem project—our analysis reveals distinctive temporal patterns in the network. We observe that the local structural hole metric within ego-networks is a strong predictor of node centrality, with nodes exhibiting a higher degree of centrality showing a greater propensity to receive incoming transactions. Furthermore, we identify specific characteristics in the local ego-networks of nodes associated with the Ethereum Foundation, the Golem project, and the broader dApps ecosystem.

We present a study of the interaction between optical fields and a two-dimensional electron system (2DES) at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface, utilizing a high-resolution terahertz spectroscopy technique. Our results reveal that the optical conductivity of the 2DES is significantly enhanced by the incident terahertz radiation. This enhancement is attributed to the excitation of the 2DES's collective plasmon mode, which is further coupled with the motion of the interface's surface atoms. Consequently, the optical conductivity exhibits a distinct terahertz-frequency resonance, which we identify as a vibrational mode of the interface. This finding demonstrates that optical fields can effectively couple with the low-dimensional quantum system at the LaAlO$_3$/STO boundary, thereby inducing surface atomic vibrations.

This paper presents a comprehensive logical system for interaction that encompasses Linear, Affine, and Classical Logics. By examining the structural properties of this system, we demonstrate that it is a substructural logic corresponding to both Linear and Affine Logic, while also serving as a sublogic of Classical Logic. Furthermore, we establish that the system functions as a B\'{e}lnap-style paraconsistent logic, which allows us to derive the characteristic logical properties of this system. Finally, we analyze the computational complexity of our system, proving that the decision problem for Linear Logic is PSPACE-complete and that the problem for Pomset Logic is NP-complete.

We introduce a novel, automated photometric redshift pipeline designed for the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields, utilizing compelled photometric data spanning 0.36 to 4.5 microns. This compelled dataset, derived from the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 surveys, is the result of a multi-year campaign involving the Hubble Space Telescope, the 10-meter Keck II telescope, and the 6.5-meter Subaru Telescope. Our pipeline employs a Bayesian approach that simultaneously estimates photometric redshifts and the probability of an object being a star. We have developed a new method for calculating photometric redshift uncertainties that incorporates uncertainties in the spectral energy distribution (SED) model, the probability density function (PDF) of the photometry, and the probability of an object being a star. This uncertainty metric is validated against spectroscopic redshifts from the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) and the COSMOS-Wide Field Survey (COSMOS-WFS). The pipeline's performance is evaluated on the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields, which contain approximately 1.5 million galaxies and 1.5 million galaxies, respectively. We demonstrate that the photometric redshifts derived from the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields are consistent with spectroscopic redshifts from the COSMOS and COSMOS-WFS surveys. This study introduces a Bayesian decision support system designed to aid planners in energy system development. The proposed methodology integrates diverse data sources, such as satellite imagery, to estimate the spatial distribution of renewable energy sources. Furthermore, it employs a Bayesian framework to derive the most probable demand scenarios for future years, incorporating uncertainty into the planning process. Additionally, the model utilizes a mixed-integer linear programming approach to determine the optimal generation capacity mix, accounting for varying demand states. The resulting optimal capacities are further refined using Bayesian techniques to generate an explicit representation of uncertainty. The paper concludes by outlining a comprehensive framework for uncertainty quantification within this planning context.

The Hartree-Fock wavefunction describes a two-body system that exhibits a specific algebraic structure, which we demonstrate gives rise to an exact representation as a matrix product state (MPS) with a three-rank form. This unique MPS structure is further shown to correspond to the three-particle density matrix's natural block diagonalization.

We introduce a minimal non-Abelian dark sector featuring a dark gauge symmetry $SU(2)_D$ and a dark fermion doublet, with the dark matter candidate being the lightest dark fermion. This model is augmented by a new $U(1)_L$ gauge symmetry that couples exclusively to Standard Model leptons. Through the mechanism of kinetic mixing between the $U(1)_L$ gauge boson and the photon, the latter acquires couplings to visible matter, thereby offering a solution to the long-standing $10^{-12}$ discrepancy in the muon's $(g-2)$ anomaly.

Global climate change is driving a surge in coastal flooding, a phenomenon that will likely worsen as sea levels rise and storm events become more severe. To address this, we introduce a novel, rapid, and physics-informed surrogate model for simulating coastal floods, utilizing neural operators to forecast water height distributions. This approach is grounded in the shallow water equations, which incorporate critical physical factors such as tides, waves, and storm surges. We trained the neural operator using a high-resolution, open-source hydrodynamic model of the Earth's coasts, leveraging the UK Met Office's high-resolution global forecast system. This system provides realistic, time-varying boundary conditions for tidal height, wave height, and storm surge levels. We validated the neural operator's efficacy by testing it on two distinct regions: the North Sea and the English Channel. Results indicate that the model can generate flood predictions in mere seconds, a stark contrast to the hours required by traditional hydrodynamic simulations. Furthermore, the model achieves high accuracy, with mean absolute errors of 0.11 meters and 0.14 meters for the North Sea and English Channel, respectively.

Cosmologlobe, a data repository for cosmological maps, was established to address the growing demand for data sharing within the field. This need was highlighted by BeyondPlanck, a collaborative initiative that gathered data from numerous missions to create a unified, open-access collection of CMB results. This paper details Cosmoglobe's architecture, which is built on a scalable, open-source data lake designed to handle the extensive datasets generated by major CMB projects. We examine the system's key features, including its robust data management, API, and support for reproducible science, alongside its commitment to facilitating future scientific endeavors. Furthermore, we analyze Cosoglobe's role in advancing BeyondPlanck and future CMB projects, emphasizing how such infrastructure promotes a culture of open data and collaboration.

This study examines a reaction-diffusion system composed of a finite transmission network with a limited number of nodes. We demonstrate that Turing instability can emerge in such systems, provided that the transmission network's topology and the reaction kinetics of the individual nodes are suitably configured. Specifically, we identify that instabilities are more readily triggered when the network features a high degree of heterogeneity. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between the spatial scale of these patterns and the reaction-diffusion parameters, noting a correlation with the system's dimensionality.

We introduce a systematic framework for the Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional Euclidean space, centered on the concept of quasiclassicality. This approach utilizes a novel set of variables, termed the "quasiclassical variables," which are constructed from the Yang-Mills fields and their functional derivatives. This transformation yields a new action that is formally exact, free of any perturbative expansion, and expressed as a functional determinant. This determinant governs the functional distribution of the Yang-Mills fields in relation to the quasiclassical variables. We demonstrate that this variable set possesses a specific functional structure, allowing the Yang-Mills theory to be recast as a theory of the variables themselves. This reformulation establishes a well-defined problem of minimizing the action, thereby enabling a transition from quantum to classical mechanics. This quasiclassical method is then applied to the instanton sector, where we derive the exact functional form of the one-instanton solution and subsequently calculate the one-loop correction to it.

We present a theoretical investigation into the polarization characteristics of single GaN/GaAs quantum wires, which exhibit a wurtzite crystal structure and intense transverse confinement. Our findings indicate that the quantum emission from these nanowires is predominantly $\sigma^+$ polarized, with a polarization degree reaching up to 99%. This exceptional polarization arises from the pronounced crystal anisotropy within the GaN system, a feature that surpasses the polarization levels observed in both GaAs and InGaAs nanowires. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the $\sigma^+$ dominance is robust against variations in the excitation beam's polarization and its angle of incidence. These outcomes underscore the potential of wurtzite quantum wires for applications requiring high-quality polarization control.

In negotiation dialogues, accurately modeling the counterpart is essential for generating high-quality responses. However, existing methods often struggle with out-of-distribution data caused by the scarcity of adaptation strategies for unseen opponents. This study introduces a framework for opponent adaptation that leverages related dialogue data to estimate counterpart preferences. By employing a dual-level attention mechanism to map similarities between opponents, the system identifies and utilizes prior negotiation interactions to train a model capable of handling previously unseen parties. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art models in terms of both dialogue outcomes and overall utility.

This study examines a light-like portion of the compactified space-time within a string theory framework. We introduce a specific string theory model where the string tension acts as a dynamical quantity, which is influenced by the compactified dimensions. We demonstrate that the dynamics of this string tension can be formulated using an effective four-dimensional theory. Furthermore, we analyze the stability of the string tension through a detailed examination of its potential energy functions, which are derived from the stringy degrees of freedom. We also explore various scenarios involving the compactified dimensions, including those with flat, spherical, and hyperbolic geometries.

Balancing binary outcomes is a fundamental challenge in various fields, including A/B testing, clinical trials, and social science research. This paper introduces a design that balances binary sequences by extending the concept of a pigeonhole design, a method originally developed for numerical data. We demonstrate that this approach achieves near-perfect balance, a property validated through simulations and a real-world online matching case study. Furthermore, we provide an online matching example where our design outperforms both the Bernoulli and T-Design methods, a superiority confirmed by both simulation results and theoretical analysis.

The Si/Al2O3 interface is essential for the creation of SiO2/Al2O3 dielectric stacks, which are critical for CMOS technology. This study employs first-principles calculations to investigate the atomic-level structure of this interface. We demonstrate that the Si/Al2O3 boundary is defined by strong covalent bonding between silicon and oxygen atoms, with ionic interactions occurring between aluminum and oxygen. This finding clarifies the long-standing debate regarding whether the interface is covalent or ionic, a distinction that is vital for comprehending the interfacial characteristics of SiO2/Al2O3 dielectric stacks.

This study introduces a new approach for estimating black hole parameters by utilizing non-linear statistical models. We specifically examine the estimation of the irreducible mass and the rotational energy of a Kerr black hole, leveraging data from an accretion disk's continuum-fitting method. Our methodology employs a non-linear regression model to approximate the analytical relationship between the observed X-ray flux and the black hole's physical properties. We compare the performance of two distinct regression techniques: (1) a polynomial model and (2) an artificial neural network. Our findings indicate that the neural network consistently outperforms the polynomial model in terms of accuracy.

This study introduces a comprehensive historical dataset spanning from 1966 to the present, covering the global container shipping industry. The new data encompasses four key areas: freight rates, shipment volumes, transactions in the newbuilding market, second-hand market activity, and scrap prices. The dataset is organized by both vessel type and size, as well as by shipping route. It is further integrated with datasets on container numbers, shipping registry locations, and specific port information. This resource is intended to facilitate research on container shipping, as well as broader investigations into international trade, financial markets, and shipping finance.

This study examines the efficacy of anomaly detection systems in real-time environments, specifically within the context of online learning. It presents a novel framework for evaluating these detectors, which incorporates a comprehensive set of metrics to gauge their performance. The authors also introduce a new metric designed to capture the impact of delayed feedback on performance. Utilizing this framework, the study conducts a thorough comparative analysis of various detectors against multiple time series datasets. The findings reveal that while existing literature often favors the ESD-based detector, a new variant utilizing the L2 norm demonstrates superior performance. Furthermore, the study highlights that the length of the detector's memory is a critical determinant of success.

This study introduces a novel, computationally efficient approach for segmenting gliomas in brain MRI images, designed to assist neurosurgeons in preoperative planning. The method utilizes a deep learning architecture based on residual U-Net, incorporating an external convolutional layer to enhance performance. To minimize computational demands, the model is trained on a subset of the dataset and employs a dynamic batch size strategy. Post-processing is handled using a combination of connected components analysis and a k-means clustering algorithm. The approach was validated on the BRATS 2018 dataset, achieving a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.89 for the tumor core and 0.91 for the enhancing tumor. These results demonstrate that the method delivers high accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art techniques while maintaining significantly reduced computational requirements.
